messages:
Avery (CEO): Thanks for a great all-hands — starting this live thread for any follow-ups on mission, positioning, market focus, competitors, and how the roadmap ties together. I'll try to answer quickly.
Priya (Head of Marketing): Two quick ones — do we have a single sentence that differentiates us vs cloud vendors? Need for page copy.
Avery (CEO): Short answer: we’re the developer-first inference platform that makes production LLMs predictable and cost-effective across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Emphasize serving economics + unified runtime.
Jordan (VP Product): Adding: call out "same API, same tooling" across hosted/dedicated/private. That line helps product folks know it's not multiple products.
Luis (Sales): From enterprise calls: customers keep asking why not just use cloud-managed endpoints (G/Azure). What's our succinct battle card?
Avery (CEO): Battle card bullets: predictable latency/SLOs, cost controls (batching/quantization recommendations), private deployment options + KMS integration, and rollout/fallback policies for reliability. We win where ops + cost matter.
Mei (Engineer): Does that mean we prioritize kernel/runtime improvements over adding model zoo models? Curious how we balance onboarding new models vs runtime perf.
Avery (CEO): We keep both. Runtime improvements are high ROI for customers (latency/cost). But model catalog + verified perf profiles are equally important for customer trust. Roadmap threads will show sequencing.
Tom (Head of Strategy): Asked earlier about TAM — are we doubling down on app infra (platform teams) or expanding PLG motion for startups? How do we prioritize sales vs self-serve?
Avery (CEO): Both. PLG for velocity and developer adoption; sales/solutions for large enterprise Dedicated/Private deals. Prioritization is usage-driven: if a customer hits security/SLA needs we trigger sales assistance.
Priya (Head of Marketing): On positioning: should we lead with "production-first" or "cost-aware" messaging? Which resonates more in pitch decks?
Avery (CEO): "Production-first" is our umbrella — under that, "cost-aware controls" is a key differentiator. Use production-first in top-level conversations, cost-aware in technical/business conversations.
Luis (Sales): Any guidance for objection handling on "we can self-host cheaper"?
Avery (CEO): Highlight total cost of ownership: engineering ops, SLAs, observability, and the time-to-value for our managed options. Also our private deployment option avoids the forklift.
Mei (Engineer): Roadmap nit: can we get a clear public doc listing what "redwood-verified" performance means per model? It's hard to justify to customers without numbers.
Jordan (VP Product): We have an internal doc; making a public one is on the near-term roadmap. Will post link here when ready.
Tom (Head of Strategy): Competitor note: a few vendors are pushing "serverless'' inference with opaque autoscaling. We should call out predictable throughput vs opaque scaling in collateral.
Avery (CEO): Agreed. Predictability beats surprises. Also, our smart routing + fallbacks are unique selling points — mention them.
All-Hands Bot: Posted slides from today's all-hands: https://redwood.internal/slides/2026-03-23-townhall (access: company SSO)
Priya (Head of Marketing): Thanks! I'll draft a 1-pager and ping Jordan + Avery for review.
Luis (Sales): I'll share top 3 enterprise objections and customer language — helps shape collateral.
Mei (Engineer): :thumbsup: small ask — can we get a signal channel for runtime perf regressions so teams see impact quickly?
Jordan (VP Product): We'll add an item to the eng-docs and spin up a perf signal channel.
Avery (CEO): Great thread — keep questions coming. If you need a deep-dive, DM me or schedule 1:1.
Priya (Head of Marketing): :raised_hands: thanks!
Mei (Engineer): :+1:
Luis (Sales): Thanks, all.
Tom (Head of Strategy): Noted.
Avery (CEO): Closing thread for now — will reopen if more follow-ups come in.
